name: Italian Game
description: Develop fast, aim your bishop at f7 and castle early. The Italian is the classic first opening: simple plans, quick development and plenty of attacking chances.

lessons.title: Giuoco Piano: build slowly
lessons.summary: The main plan: c3 and d3, castle, then expand.

moves.note: Grab the center and open lines for your queen and light-squared bishop.
Black claims an equal share of the center.
Develop toward the center and attack the e5 pawn right away.
Black defends e5 with a developing move.
The Italian bishop. It eyes f7, the square only Black's king protects.
Black mirrors you and aims the bishop at your f2.
Prepare d4 for a big center, and take the d4 square away from Black's knight.
Black develops and puts pressure on your e4 pawn.
Protect e4 calmly. You keep a solid center and avoid early tactics.
Black supports e5 and opens a path for the light-squared bishop.
Castle. Your king is safe and your rook can join the game.
Black castles too. Both sides have finished the first phase.
The rook backs up e4 and gets ready for a later d4 push.

lessons.title: Two Knights: the quiet d3
lessons.summary: Answer 3...Nf6 by protecting e4 and castling.

moves.note: Take the center with your king's pawn.
Black answers in kind.
Develop and attack e5.
Black defends.
Aim the bishop at f7.
The Two Knights Defense: Black attacks e4 at once instead of developing the bishop first.
Defend e4 with a pawn. No gambits needed, and your position stays sound.
A modest square for the bishop. Black wants to castle quickly.
Castle before starting any action in the center.
Black's king is safe too.
Put the rook behind your e-pawn, where the center may open.
Black reinforces e5.
Same plan as the Giuoco Piano: prepare d4 and give your bishop a retreat to c2.

lessons.title: Strike with c3 and d4
lessons.summary: Hit the center while Black's pieces aren't ready.

moves.note: Take the center.
Black matches you.
Develop and attack e5.
Black defends.
Aim the bishop at f7.
Black's bishop aims at f2.
Prepare d4.
Black attacks e4.
Strike now! Two pawns in the center hit e5 and gain space.
Black takes, so your center can't roll forward with tempo.
Recapture with the c-pawn and keep two pawns side by side in the center.
Black's bishop escapes with check instead of retreating.
Block with your bishop and offer a trade.
Black trades bishops.
Recapture with the b1 knight, developing another piece.
Black hits back in the center before you can play e5.
Take. The e-file opens toward Black's uncastled king.
Black recaptures with the knight, which sits well on d5.
Pressure d5 and f7 at the same time. Black has to be careful.

lessons.title: Don't fall for 3...Nd4
lessons.summary: Trade the knight off and castle. Don't grab e5.

moves.note: Take the center.
Black matches you.
Develop and attack e5.
Black defends.
Aim the bishop at f7.
A trap! If you grab e5 with Nxe5, Black's queen jumps to g5 with nasty threats.
Trade off the annoying knight instead. Simple and strong.
Black recaptures, but the pawn on d4 is now a target.
Castle and bring your rook closer. You're ahead in development.
Black develops and attacks e4.
Defend e4 with the rook. Your pieces work together.
Black blocks the e-file and frees the bishop.
Attack d4 to open lines for your pieces.
Black takes.
Recapture and develop your last minor piece. You have a big lead in development.
